---
name: comm-preserve-visual-design
description: Use when creating or substantially redesigning a user interface, implementing an approved visual reference, or verifying visual conformance before completion.
---

# Visual conformance

Inputs: actual reference/version, approvals, delegated decisions.

1. Inspect the reference. Preserve its location/version, layout, action hierarchy,
   visibility, responsiveness and essential states in an authorized permanent
   project record. Apply latest explicit changes; never mix versions. Missing
   reference: request it; pause dependent work only.
2. Separate requirements, structure, appearance and technical approvals.
   Wireframes approve shown structure, not unseen styling. Before implementing
   unapproved appearance, present an accessible concrete design covering key
   states and responsiveness; obtain approval unless delegated. Opening queued
   proves neither viewing nor approval.
3. Preserve authorizations. Obtain approval for material deviations before
   implementation. Direct instructions authorize named changes; conformance fixes
   and delegated details need no repeated approval.
4. Compare actual renders with the reference at relevant sizes/states. Verify
   behavior, structure and appearance separately; functional tests or screenshots
   alone do not prove conformance.
5. Report evidence, approved deviations and unverified aspects. Unapproved
   material mismatches prevent full-completion claims.

Before token/literal choices read [semantics](references/value-semantics.md).

Before preserving records follow
`harness/common/skills/comm-preserve-harness-knowledge/SKILL.md`; evidence also
follows `harness/common/skills/comm-protect-harness-evidence/SKILL.md`.

Done: conformance or explicit gaps; preserve workflow and project-specific business rules.

# Bind values by visual intent

Before replacing a literal or binding a shared token, establish its semantic role
and approved reference/version. Equal current values do not establish a shared
contract. History helps identify changes, not decide which design is correct.

Compare suitable choices within project design-system constraints:
- Reuse a token when its role and intended future variation match the element.
- Propose a separate semantic token when an independent role justifies maintenance.
- A fixed value may preserve a versioned approved prototype when project rules
  allow it; it is not automatically an error or an exemption from those rules.

Choose by intended behavior and evidence, not literal/token quotas or a blanket
"token changed, so literal is right" rule. Apply the skill's existing approval
and delegation conditions for material deviations; verify affected renders/states.
Reference provenance belongs to the existing reference record; browser artifact
identity and prototype serving use comm-prepare-browser-check. Do not duplicate
those algorithms or automatically update the reference to latest.
